research_inputs.finding: Execution provenance should connect evidence, tool outputs, memory, observations, claims, actions, and agents in typed traces and support verification, safety, audit, debugging, and recovery.
research_inputs.used_for: typed proposal steps, evidence digest binding, and explicit certificate record

research_inputs.finding: The Proposal-Certification-Execution architecture argues that generated traces should execute only after a policy machine certifies them; local action permission does not imply trace permission.
research_inputs.used_for: pre-execution certification, cumulative budgets, approvals, and no-execution certificate semantics

research_inputs.finding: Agent orchestration should use the lowest complexity that meets requirements, bound iteration loops, and use deterministic sequencing and maker-checker gates where appropriate.
research_inputs.used_for: bounded steps, deterministic dependency ordering, and explicit high-risk approval gates

research_inputs.finding: Agent benchmark validity depends on the complete environment, information flow, scoring, and verification protocol; exposed artifacts and feedback can create score-relevant shortcuts.
research_inputs.used_for: evidence binding, policy fencing, and explicit limits on what certification establishes

limitations: Certification is bounded deterministic policy checking, not a formal proof of all external-world properties.
The module does not call a model, browser, tool, network, accelerator, or side effect.
Caller-supplied policy, capability, approval, and evidence registries must be provisioned by a trusted control-plane boundary; the module does not create their authority.
The local benchmark measures Python control-plane overhead only.
This evidence does not claim AGI, autonomous execution safety, browser safety, robotics capability, or production approval.
